summary: This defines a Room class: a small blueprint that bundles a room's name together with its length and width. It is a domain class, meaning it models one thing from the real world and offers methods to read and change its data.

lines.text: Declares the blueprint. Every room object created from this class carries its own name, length, and width.
Stores the room's name, such as "Kitchen". Marking it private means code outside the class cannot touch it directly.
Holds the length as a decimal number, since room dimensions are rarely whole numbers.
A no-argument constructor that creates an empty room, to be filled in later with the setter methods.

lines.code: public Room(String name, double length, double width) {
lines.text: A second constructor that accepts all three values at once, so a fully described room can be built in a single step.
The parameter and the field share the name name, so this.name makes it clear that the field is the one being assigned.
A getter: the controlled way for other classes to read the private name field.
A setter: the controlled way to change the name after the object exists. Keeping fields private and going through methods like this is called encapsulation.
Announces that the method below replaces one inherited from Object. The compiler will complain if the signature does not match, which catches typos.
Defines what the room looks like as text, so printing a Room shows its data instead of a cryptic memory reference.
Begins assembling the description; the + at the end of each line continues building one long string.
Wraps the name in single quotes. The '\'' is an escaped quote character, which is how Java writes a literal apostrophe.
